analysis.text: Has lethal combination of size and athleticism.  Runs the floor very well.  Dominant on the defensive end.  Excellent shot blocker and rebounder.   Alters so many shots that his numbers alone don't do him justice. Great hands.  Soft touch from inside and a developing jumper.  Very good passer out of the post.  Smart kid.

Doesn't dominate the way you'd expect him to.  Can be almost too nice at times.  Doesn't have the killer instinct, though he started playing with more passion in the second half of the season.  Post moves still need work.  Wrist fracture sidelined him for the start of the season at Ohio State.  His right wrist is still very stiff, forcing him to shoot free throws with his left hand for much of the season.

Oden announced on April 20 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft and hiring an agent, ending his college eligibility.

Oden made a big impact as a freshman in Columbus.
(Michael Hickey/WireImage.com)
Top 2

The consensus No. 1 pick in the draft despite Kevin Durant's amazing season. Draws comparisons to Tim Duncan, Patrick Ewing and David Robinson. He may not be spectacular, but most NBA GMs believe he'll immediately be one of the top two centers in the league. His strong performance in the NCAA title game gave us a glimmer of what he's capable of, going for 25 points, 12 boards and 4 blocks.
Tim Duncan meets Patrick Ewing

He's been atop our Top 100 since last July and has never moved. He's the best player in the draft when you factor in position, defensive presence, ability to become an offensive force. Kevin Durant was a hot option, too. But the Blazers are on the path to an NBA title with Oden, Brandon Roy and LaMarcus Aldridge. Look for them to trade Zach Randolph soon to continue the rebuilding.
Oden completes young Portland nucleus.

Durant has it all:  size, length, athleticism and a sweet-looking jump shot.  Can play multiple positions on the floor.  Very active. Aggressive.  Looks to score and can kill you inside and out.  Zips up and down the floor.  NBA range on his 3-pointer. Quick release and perfect mechanics on the jump shot. He prefers to play outside in, but he's proven he can rebound and block shots.  Great hands.  Good ball handler. Virtually unstoppable on the offensive end.

Strength.  Durant's body keeps him from being one of the most complete forwards in the game.  He needs to add 15 to 20 pounds of muscle.  Given his slight frame, that could be an issue.  Doesn't play defense with any intensity.

Durant made his mark quickly in Austin.
(Jim Redman/WireImage.com )

Durant declared for the 2007 NBA Draft on April 10th. He will hire an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Top 2

Some scouts are calling him a mixture of Kevin Garnett and Dirk Nowitzki.  Others say he's the most complete college player they've ever seen.  His play as a freshman has been epic.   Right now he's the consensus No. 2 pick in the draft behind Greg Oden with a small minority of GMs saying he could beat out Oden for the No. 1 pick.
Kevin Garnett meets Dirk Nowitzki

The easiest pick in the draft. Durant is one of the most amazing scorers we've ever seen in a big man. He also can rebound and plays with amazing intensity. He's going to be the most entertaining guy to watch in the draft. He'll lead a revival in Seattle alongside new GM Sam Presti and the guy who the Sonics will take at No. 5 -- Jeff Green.
Most entertaining player in the draft.

Horford has the tools to be a great NBA player.  He's long, athletic and has a great NBA body.  He's got excellent toughness and doesn't shy away from banging in the paint.  Excellent passer for a big man. His per minute numbers in the point, rebounding and shot-blocking departments have scouts drooling.  Gets up and down the floor.  Good motor.  Very quick for a big guy.  Excellent basketball IQ. Improving midrange game.
His offensive skills in the post are improving, but he still needs a lot of work.  Gets into foul trouble a lot due to overaggressiveness.  Plays a little robotic.
Horford announced on April 5 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft and forgoing his senior season of college. His father, Tito, played in the NBA.
Top 10

Horford has the body and skill set needed to play in the NBA right away. He was a beast as a shot blocker and rebounder, and he impresses scouts with his ability to handle the ball under pressure in the open court.  Horford needs a little more polish on the offensive end, but he has everything else you want in a power player -- the length, strength, motor, athleticism and basketball IQ that coaches crave in a power forward. His game still has room to grow, but right now he looks like a lock for the Top 10 and a potential Top 5 prospect thanks to an excellent NCAA tournament.

Horford has the power needed for NBA play.
(Brad Wilder/WireImage.com)

He's the third best player in the draft, so you can't fault the Hawks here. He's better than any other power forward they have. He could be a poor man's Karl Malone. The Hawks did need a point guard, and I think Mike Conley was worth the No. 3 pick in the draft, so I would've taken Conley. But -- unlike Shelden Williams last year -- this isn't a bad pick.
Good pick, but would have chosen Conley.

Has great length, athleticism and a crazy motor that runs non stop. More skilled than you think. An excellent passer for a big man. Beats everyone up and down the floor. He's always around the ball and is an excellent shot blocker.

Noah has the ability to do a little of everything -- he can score inside, block shots, crash the glass on both ends, handle the ball on the break, make passes that only point guards are supposed to know how to make. In short, he's everywhere ... sort of a 7-foot Kirilenko.

He's too thin and doesn't seem to have the frame to hold much more weight.  He's very raw offensively and gets most of his points on dunks and offensive rebounds.  Footwork in the post needs work.  Has virtually no range on the jump shot.  What position does he play in the pros?
Noah announced on April 5 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA draft and forgoing his senior season of college. Noah is the son of Yannick Noah, the former tennis star from France.
Lottery

Noah capped an amazing NCAA tournament in 2006 with a near-perfect championship game -- a Carmelo Anthony-esque breakout that had propelled him into contention to be the No. 1 pick in the draft. However, he's been unable to duplicate that magic this season with any consistency.  While he's still regarded as a lottery pick, the buzz that he gained last season has quieted.  A quieter NCAA tournament this year didn't kill his stock, but he no longer looks like the best prospect on his own team.

The buzz may have quieted on Noah, but he still boasts a variety of skills.
(Rex Brown/WireImage.com)
Anderson Varejao meets Andrei Kirilenko

The Bulls have been after Noah for awhile. Though he doesn't fit a need, he does fit the system. He plays with the energy that Bulls head coach Scott Skiles demands. I'm not sure they can play him and Ben Wallace together, but as Wallace gets older, he'll be a good replacement.
Doesn't fit needs, but fits the system.

One of the steadiest point guards in the country.  A pure point who always thinks team first.  Doesn't turn the ball over very often.  Excellent at handling pressure.  Has the ability to slash to the basket.  NBA body. Very good athlete. Good lateral quickness and quick hands make him an excellent on-the-ball defender.
Inconsistent jump shot with little to no NBA 3-point range.   Can be too unselfish at times.

Conley has run the show nicely in Columbus.
(AP Photo/Terry Gilliam)

Conley announced on April 20th that he will enter his name into the 2007 NBA Draft. Best friends with Ohio State center Greg Oden.
Top 10

Conley quickly asserted himself as the best young college point guard in the country. His leadership for Ohio State in the NCAA tournament took him out of the shadow of Greg Oden and created some serious draft buzz. He's become the darling of NBA scouts looking for steady, pure point guards who can control a team.  Look for him to be the first point guard off the board.

Conley is the best point guard in the draft and the Grizzlies needed a point guard, so it's a good pick. Put him on the floor with Pau Gasol, Mike Miller and Rudy Gay and the Grizzlies will be much better next year. I'm not sure they're a playoff team, but they will be respectable.
Needed a PG and got the best in draft.

Long forward who has what Bill Simmons likes to call "nuclear athleticism."  He's almost impossible to stop in the open court.  The lefty is unusually quick for his size meaning he can take his guy off the dribble and guard just about everyone but centers on the floor.  His super long arms means he plays bigger than he looks.  Excellent passer. His perimeter game is still developing, but it's not bad.  Young is another great kid.  He's a hard worker and gets great grades.

What position does he play?  Scouts see him as a bit of tweener. He needs to add another 15 to 20 pounds of muscle.  He's very thin and can get pushed around.  A little too perimeter oriented for his size and his lack of a consistent jump shot at the moment. Can't go right.

Packing on muscle could help Young's stock.
(Scott Thornton/WireImage.com)

Young announced on April 24 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft. Young announced on June 18th that he was staying in the draft.
Lottery to mid first round

Young is another big-time prospect whose upside is only limited by questions about position and strength and body development issues.  He's had a solid freshman season for Georgia Tech, but most of his draft stock has to do with upside. He's a late lottery to mid first round selection.
Al Harrington

This is a small surprise. On talent, Young may have had the most upside of anyone left on the board. He isn't ready yet, but he is an excellent athlete, an emerging shooter and a hard worker. He should be a great complement to Andre Iguodala.
Small surprise but athleticism and work ethic are there.

Scoring machine combo guard with enough size,  strength and skill to play both the one and the two in the pros.  A good athlete. He's at his best off the dribble and is an excellent finisher around the basket.  He has a great combination of strength and quickness that makes him virtually unstoppable.  Gets to the line frequently, averaging more than 8 free throws a game.  A streaky outside shooter, but he does have NBA 3-point range.

The biggest knock against him is the competition he plays against on a nightly basis.  Eastern Washington isn't a great team and Stuckey carries most of the load which may enhance his offensive production a bit.  He needs to be more consistent shooting the ball from long range.
Stuckey declared for the NBA Draft on April 25th.  He has hired an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Lottery to mid first round

He's considered a serious draft sleeper by some NBA scouts who think he has legit mid  first round potential. With a number of young combo guards (read 
Randy Foye, Ben Gordon, Monta Ellis, etc.) thriving in the NBA, Stuckey seems to have the tools to follow in their footsteps.  "If he were playing in the ACC, he'd be a top 10 pick," one scout said. "The question will be, will NBA teams penalize him because he dominates the Big Sky?"

Stuckey is one of this year's sleepers.
(Matt Brown/Icon SMI)

Randy Foye

We had Stuckey in every mock draft. Stuckey is an excellent combo guard who put pressure on the defense. He's kind of like Randy Foye. With Lindsey Hunter nearly ready to hang it up, Stuckey will eventually fill his role. He'll be a great fit in Detroit.
Perfect fit and ready to fill his role.

Do-it-all forward who can shoot, pass, rebound and lock someone down on the defensive end.  Good athlete.  Long arms.  Good strength. Point forward skills make him one of those rare big men who makes everyone around him better.  Excellent basketball IQ.  Can score in the post.
An inconsistent scorer.  Streaky shooter. Can be unselfish to a fault.  A bit of a tweener between the three and the four.  While he does everything well, he isn't great at any one thing.

If Green continues to develop, he'll be a good first-round prospect.
(AP Photo/Nick Wass)

Green announced on April 13 that he would declare for the 2007 NBA Draft. Green announced on May 23 that he was hiring an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Top 10

Scouts love his versatility and all-around game.  But he doesn't really have one standout skill which hurts him a bit.  After a rocky start, played excellent in the second half of the season.  A strong NCAA tournament was offset a little by disappearing in the Final Four game versus Ohio State.

The Celtics traded the No. 5 pick, Delonte West and Wally Szczerbiak to the Sonics for Ray Allen. Green has been one of the hottest names in the draft the past few weeks. Some scouts say he has a chance to be a Scottie Pippen-like player in the pros. He's a great passer and very versatile. He may be the perfect wingman for Kevin Durant.
Perfect wingman for Kevin Durant.

Long, lanky swingman with great size for the two.  Good athlete.  A real game changer on the defensive end of the floor. Long arms allow him to be a very tough defender.  Gets a lot of steals.  Excels in the open court. Excellent finisher in transition. Good motor and pretty unselfish. Decent set shooter, especially from 3-point range though he's been very inconsistent in that department this season.  Good on the offensive boards.
Still figuring out how to shoot off the dribble. Needs to add strength to his thin frame. Ballhandling is just fair. Very inconsistent.
Brewer announced on April 5 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft and forgoing his senior season of college.
Top 10

An excellent NCAA tournament this season helped Brewer's stock perhaps more than anyone else. He got  hot from the perimeter, answering his critics who said he couldn't shoot. His size, versatility and defense are elite for a player at his position.  If NBA teams believe he'll also score, he's a Top 10 pick.

Brewer's no-look skills include dunking.
(AP Photo/John Bazemore)

Tayshaun Prince

The Wolves didn't get KG traded, but they did grab one of the most versatile players in the draft. He's an amazing defender and an emerging offensive force. He can play at the 2 or 3, but most likely will be in the backcourt with Randy Foye.
Still have KG and added elite defender.

A long, athletic forward who is very skilled. Explosive leaper with good lateral quickness. He has long arms (7-foot-4 wingspan) and big hands, which allows him to play even bigger than he actually is. Excellent shooter and ballhandler.  Fundamentally very sound.  Excellent basketball IQ. Has really improved his rebounding. Hard worker.
Needs to add strength, especially to his upper body.  Needs to play more physically.  Needs to work on his post-up game.  Not a great shot-blocker.  More of a face-the-basket type of 4.

Yi's team, the Guangdong Tigers, announced in November 2006 that Yi will be released to enter the 2007 NBA Draft.  While he's listed as being born in 1987, many scouts believe that he's actually born in 1984 making him 23 ... not 19.  That's a big difference in NBA development terms. Is averaging 24.8 ppg, 11.4 rpg while shooting 57 percent from the field for the Guangdong Tigers this season.
Top 10

Yi is the best international prospect in the draft this year.  He has a ton of experience playing in international competitions and at the highest level in China.  Given his upside and size he's a lock for the Top 10 pick who could go as high as No. 3 according to several NBA executives.

Yi's skills just might be too good to keep him in Guangdong.
(AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill)

Toni Kukoc

Milwaukee's going to have a fight on their hands. Yi's representatives are saying that he won't play in Milwaukee and will try to force a trade. The Bucks know it's an uphill battle, but felt he was the best talent left on the board and say they want to keep him. I'll say this -- it took a lot of courage for the Bucks to do what they did. We'll see how it turns out.
Tricky pick, Bucks want him, Yi wants out.

After two years in Lawrence, Wright might be ready for the NBA in 2007. (Barry Taylor/WireImage.com)

Great athlete with very long arms that allow him to play much bigger. He
plays with great energy, is a terrific defender and is an excellent passer for a player his size. Has the ability to be a point forward in the pros. He runs the floor very well, rebounds and just has a nose for the ball.

His jump shot is still a question mark.  He has some consistency from 12 to 15 feet but really lacks any range beyond that.  Almost unselfish to a fault.  Doesn't always dominate the way he could. Scouts wonder exactly what position he'll play in the pros.

Wright told reporters on March 25 that he was returning to Kansas for his junior season.  He said the chances of him playing at Kansas next year were "100%."  However, he changed his mind and declared for the 2007 NBA Draft on April 9. Wright will hire an agent soon, ending his college eligibility.
Top 10

Wright may be the most versatile player in the draft.  He can guard and play four positions on the floor ... but he needs to develop a more consistent offensive game. Look for him to be a Top 10 pick who could go as high as No. 3 depending on who's picking in the draft.
A more aggressive and athletic Boris Diaw

I love Julian Wright. I think he's been underrated all year -- he does so many things well. He's not a great shooter, but he's a guy who makes teams better. He'll be very good running the floor with Chris Paul. I'm a little surprised they passed on Nick Young, who fit a need, but Wright was the best player left on the board.
Underrated and does a lot of things well.

Skilled big man with advanced low-post moves for a kid his age.  Can score with either hand around the basket. Excellent shooter who can play the high post and work the pick and pop.   Good passer for a big man.  Excellent basketball IQ. As fundamentally sound as any big man in the country.
Needs to add strength to play in the post.  Just an average athlete and rebounder.  Struggles as a defender at times against more athletic opponents.

Hawes is delivering good numbers for the Huskies.
(AP Photo/ Mark Avery)

Hawes announced on April 5th that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft. Hawes, will not hire an agent to preserve his college eligibility. Nephew of Steve Hawes, who averaged 8.4 ppg over 10 NBA seasons (1974-85).
Lottery

Hawes doesn't have the athletic upside of many of the top prospects in the draft, but his basketball skill and size should translate into a very solid NBA career.  Think Vlade Divac.  At this point, Hawes is looking like a legit lottery pick if he decides to stay in the draft.
Vlade Divac

Hawes is basically Brad Miller Jr. He's a great offensive player in the post and an excellent passer. And he's pretty tough. But he doesn't rebound and he's not a great athlete. He's not ready yet, but down the road, he has a chance to be a good, though not great, center.
Good but not great future center.

Wright is a super long, athletic big man who spends most of his time around the basket.  Runs the floor very well and knows how to get to the rim.  Very quick and explosive.  Can be a smothering defender.

Strength is a major issue.  He needs at least 20 pounds or more to play his position in the pros.  Lacks great perimeter skills at the moment.  At times he plays with a lack intensity.  Will float at times.  His rebounding and shot-blocking numbers are a little disappointing considering what he's capable of.

Brandan Wright has athleticism to spare, but needs more power.
(Kevin C. Cox/WireImage.com)

Wright announced on April 23 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft.
Top 10

On potential, he has the chance to be a NBA All-Star.  And so far he's proven that with a strong freshman season for Carolina. He has all the tools to be great and his strong performance in the NCAA tournament should guarantee him a spot in the Top 10 with a chance to go as high as the No. 3 pick in the draft.
LaMarcus Aldridge meets Sam Perkins

[Traded to Golden State] It appears that the Bobcats have traded this pick to Golden State for Jason Richardson. Michael Jordan has been saying for weeks that he didn't want a rookie but wanted an established player who could help put the Bobcats in the playoffs. Richardson is coming off a great playoff run for the Warriors and fits a big need for the Bobcats at the 2. For the Warriors, the deal clears cap room, rids the team of a logjam at the 2 and gives them a young, athletic 4 to pair in the frontcourt with Andris Biedrins.
Tons of upside, but a work in progress.

He really has it all -- athleticism, ballhandling, shooting touch (with NBA 3-point range) and active defense. He has the ability to play both the one and the two because of his excellent floor vision, increasing his value.  He's got a great vertical and a long wingspan.  Good lateral quickness.  Excellent basketball IQ.  Fearless.  He takes it to the defense.  Plays above the rim.

Strength is the biggest issue.  He looks very frail and needs to add a lot of muscle to his wiry frame.  Average first step means he too often settles for jumpers.  Not a great shooter off the dribble.

Fernandez might need some body work to thrive in the NBA. (Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP/Getty Images)

Fernandez declared for the 2005 Draft but withdrew his name when he wasn't
guaranteed to be a first-round pick. Plays for DKV Joventut in Spain. Averaged 15.8 ppg and shooting 43 percent from three in 25 mpg in the Euroleague this season.
Late first to early second

He fell out of good graces with many GMs last season.  He's got all the tools, but GMs are waiting for him to put them together and praying he works on that body. His strong season in Euroleague play has helped his stock, but he's still stuck on the first-round bubble.
Derek Anderson

The Suns, for the fourth straight year, have traded or sold their pick. Maybe they should just dump their entire scouting department. Last year the Blazers bought the Suns' pick late in the first round and took a player from Spain, Sergio Rodriguez. This year they get another Spanish sensation, Rudy Fernandez. Fernandez is a really good value here. He is athletic, can play both guard positions and has become an excellent shooter. He had a fantastic year in Spain last year. He has some contract issues that may keep him out of the NBA for a few years. But long term, this could be a great pickup for the Blazers.
Long term, Portland gets great value.

Thornton's athleticism is a plus, but his rebounding needs work.
(Photo by Paul Abell/Getty Images)

Super-athletic forward. Plays with great intensity. Big-time scorer. Excellent perimeter defender. Has improved his free throw shooting dramatically this year. Also has shown some shot-blocking ability this season. His rebounding and three-point shooting have also increased this year.

Not the smartest player in the country.  Bogs down a bit in the half court game when asked to execute an offense.  Is a bit of a tweener.  Plays the 4 in college but will have to move to the 3 in the pros.  Streaky perimeter shooter. So-so rebounder for his size and athletic ability.
Lottery

A few big games against Florida and North Carolina this season have given him some buzz.  And his consistent play has begun to dissipate questions about his position, basketball IQ and and lack of rebounding.  Right now he's looking more and more like a lottery pick.
Shawn Marion

Interesting pick for the Clippers. He's kind of like Corey Maggette, which means it's far from a good fit. He doesn't have a great basketball IQ, but he is the second-best athlete in the draft. And they will love the energy he plays with. A wrist injury may have hurt his stock a bit.
Low basketball IQ, but a great athlete.

A smooth, scoring swingman who does a little bit of everything.  Good athlete with long arms and explosiveness.  Skilled in just about every area of the game. Nice form on his jump shot, both the long and midrange jumper.  Good rebounder.  Game looks like it comes easy to him.

Intensity.  Young doesn't always seem to possess that killer instinct on either end of the floor.  Disappears at times. Work ethic has been questioned.  At times in the past, he has played out of control. He also needs to hit the weight room.
Young announced on April 18th that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft.
Lottery to mid first round

Young has the potential to be a lottery pick with his skills.  But scouts are still waiting for him to put it all together consistently.  The skills wow you, and his consistent play for the Trojans this season have moved him solidly into the first round.

Young could soar into the lottery.
(Anthony J Causi/Icon SMI)
Really good value here. The Wizards needed a potent 2 guard to pair with Gilbert Arenas in the backcourt. Young was a little underrated, and he should thrive in the Wizards run-and-gun offense.
Good value, should thrive in Wizard offense.

Splitter's got an NBA body, though he still needs to make it stronger. Most scouts agree that his defense is ahead of his offense right now. He's an excellent rebounder and shot blocker. He does have a nice handle and a good, but not great, jumper. He's very long and runs the floor well. He's a good, but not great, athlete.  He's fearless and doesn't mind contact in the paint. His athleticism and coordination are also improving. Despite his youth, scouts say Splitter plays like a 25-year-old.
What position does he play? Probably power forward, but he needs to improve his inside scoring if that's the case. A little more strength is needed for him to make the transition to the center.

A native of Brazil playing in Spain for one of the top teams in Europe, Tau Ceramica. Averaging 10.9 ppg and 5.9 rpg in his first 18 Euroleague games of 2006-07 season. Averaged 9.5 ppg and 4.6 rpg in Euroleague play in 2005-06. Splitter was terrific for the Brazilian national team. He scored 25 points for Brazil in the gold medal game of the 2005 FIBA Americas Men's World Championship Qualifying Tournament.
Time to put down the multi-color ball -- the NBA wants you, Tiago.
(AP Photo/Ramon Espinosa)

Averaged 13.2 ppg and 8.6 rpg for the tournament. Splitter declared for the past three drafts. He withdrew in 2004 after he couldn't secure a promise in the lottery. In 2005, he received interest from lottery teams, but concerns about a massive buyout scared teams away from making a promise. So he withdrew again from the draft. Same thing in 2006.
Lottery to mid first round

His stock was hurt in previous drafts over serious questions about whether an NBA team would be able to buy him out of his contract with TAU.  Now he's in automatically because of his age.  This year his stock has taken another hit because of his lack of improvement, however his play in the playoffs has improved dramatically.  Splitter doesn't have a buyout  from his contract with Tau until the summer of 2008, so there's a chance a team will have to wait on him a year.  Given the uncertainty about his future and his up and down year, Splitter's stock is still in flux between the late lottery and mid first round.

Great pick for the Spurs. They get a guy who would've gone 10 to 15 picks higher had he been able to come to the NBA right away this year. The Spurs have to wait a year, but when they get him, they'll get a big man who can play in the middle for the next 10 years. Splitter won't be a star, but he'll be a solid pro.
Have to wait a year, but he'll be ready.

Fundamentally sound big man with excellent hands.  Good strength and size for his position.  Plays physical. A number of excellent back to the basket moves.  Good passer out of the double team.  Great basketball IQ.
A below average NBA athlete.  Can be plodding at times.  Plays below the rim which hurts both his rebounding and shot blocking numbers.  Slow.  Has struggled with weight issues in the past.
Brother of Grizzlies star Pau Gasol.  Averaging 10.8 ppg and 5.6 rpg in 23 mpg for Akasvayu Girona in the Spanish ACB league.
Late first to early second
Some NBA international scouts think that, with proper conditioning he could be a valuable player in the pros given his size and skill set.  A real bubble first rounder.
Pau Gasol's brother isn't a great prospect, but he does take up space in the middle. He probably stays in Spain for another year or two.
Pau's bro will stay in Spain for now.
Skilled BIG man with a feathery touch in the post.  Excellent athleticism for someone so big.  Polished low-post scorer and good rebounder.  Has a real feel for the game.

Weight is obviously a huge issue.  It bothered him in the NCAA tournament and scouts are concerned as he gets older it will take its toll on his body and he'll have a harder time keeping the weight off.  His dramatic weight loss in the summer of 2007 gives hope that this may be a problem of the past.  Though the latest word out of LSU is that Davis has gained much of that weight back.
Announced on March 21st that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft and hiring an agent, ending his college eligibility. Nickname is "Big Baby."
Late first to early second

The knock on Davis last season centered on his lack of height and conditioning. Davis had been able to hide those faults this year somewhat thanks to his weight loss.  He's more explosive now which allows him to play bigger.  Still, scouts are concerned a big paycheck may come with another big weight gain.  Now that he's in the draft, scouts expect him to shed most of the weight he's gained over the last month again ... but the lingering question remains ... can he keep it off?

Davis' size is an asset, unless of course he's really too big.
(Rex Brown/WireImage.com)

Oliver Miller
The Celtics got this pick from the Sonics and land "Big Baby." Put him on the floor with Al Jefferson and you have a beefy frontline that can score. Nice pick.
Nice pick adds to Boston frontline.
Draft profile coming soon ...
Second round to undrafted
Landry is a tough guy who gave Greg Oden all he could handle in the Big 10. He's a little undersized, but he's a bruiser.
A little undersized, but is still tough.
Long, athletic forward with excellent explosiveness.  Good strength.  Solid rebounder. Excellent running the floor.  Good finisher around the basket. Developing mid range game.
Needs to improve his perimeter game and ball handling skills.  A bit of a tweener.  Lacks a great motor.  Questionable shot selection.
Early entry candidate.
Late first to early second

Chandler surprised with his decision to enter and stay in the draft.  Has a ton of raw athletic talent, but has yet to produce in a serious way on the court.  There's talk that the Knicks are in love with him at No. 23.   He's yet to workout for a team, citing an injury, so maybe there is something to it.

The Renaldo Balkman pick shocked us last year. We weren't going to get caught off-guard again ... and were the first to report Chandler to the Knicks several weeks ago. Chandler is an excellent athlete and has good size. But he doesn't have a great motor and was just a so-so college player. Should be a better player in the pros.
Better suited for NBA than he was in college.

Big-time scorer who does it all.  He's an excellent shooter with a legit midrange jumper.  He's also an excellent penetrator who can get to the basket and finish. Has a quick first step. Already has an NBA body and athleticism.   Explosive leaper.  Excellent rebounder for a little guy.

He's a bit undersized for the position.   Given his explosiveness, he should be getting to the line more.  Ends up, too often, settling for jumpers.  His assist-to-turnover rate shows that he can play a little out of control.  Not a great ballhandler, passer or free throw shooter.
Cook announced on April 20 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA draft.  Cook has not hired an agent, preserving his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

Cook came on strong at the start of the season, but then took a back seat to Greg Oden when Oden returned from injury. Still, scouts think he's an excellent prospect as a scorer in a Ben Gordon type of mold. Looks like a mid to late first round pick right now.

Cook could be a big-time scorer at the pro level. (John Sommers/Icon SMI)

Ben Gordon

[Traded to Miami] The Heat swapped picks with the Sixers and will end up with Cook. The team knows it needs athleticism and Cook helps in that department. He's also an excellent shooter. But Cook is not ready to help right now. He doesn't have strong ball-handling skills or much of a midrange game. So I'm not sure how well he fits behind Dwyane Wade and Dorell Wright.
Weak handling skills, but an great shooter.

Pass first point guard with good floor vision and the ability to get to the basket.  He's a good finisher around the basket and has a solid mid range jumper.  Makes good decisions on the floor.  Committed defender.
Not overly athletic.  Doesn't have deep range on his jump shot.
Declared for the 2007 NBA draft on April 20.  He announced on June 15 that he's hiring an agent and staying in the draft.
Late first to early second
Sessions isn't great at any one thing, but solid in just about every area.  He's a playmaker who could help a team in the second round.
A solid point guard who knows how to get to the basket. He impressed in workouts and may have a job if Mo Williams leaves this summer via free agency.
May get a job if Mo Williams departs.

Big-time scorer with a beautiful jump shot.  Is a dead-eye mid-range shooter. Has added a  3-point shot to his arsenal.  Has a good feel for the game and isn't afraid to take the last shot. Has the ability to put the ball on the floor and get to the rim. Good defender as long as he isn't asked to be physical.  Excellent conditioning.

He's an average athlete, at best.  Isn't very quick and is not an explosive leaper.  Scouts claim he's probably closer to 6-foot-4 which makes him a little undersized for the two, though he does have a long wingspan.  Doesn't have deep range, the longer NBA three point line may pose a problem for him.

Afflalo declared for the 2007 NBA Draft on April 10th.  Because this is the second time Afflalo has declared, he is ineligible to return back to college. Declared for the 2006 NBA Draft but withdrew after not getting serious interest in the first round.
Late first to early second

Afflalo doesn't have the athleticism or size to compete against long, athletic players. He's likely to have similar problems in the pros which is why he's on the first round bubble, despite having a terrific junior year.
A shorter version of Raja Bell

Afflalo is a Joe Dumars type of player -- a tough, hard-nosed guard who plays great defense and has a nice midrange game. But Afflalo isn't a great athlete, and I wonder how he'll fit on the roster with the Pistons drafting another guard, Rodney Stuckey, at No. 15.
Tough, hard-nosed, but not a great athlete.

Great basketball IQ and feel guy who just knows how to win.  His best attribute is the passion and energy he brings to every game. Excellent rebounder for his size.  Big hands and long arms make up for his lack of size.  Solid midrange jumper.  Good effort defender.

He lacks an NBA position and NBA athleticism.  Plays more like a four, but is the size of a small forward.  Not a deep three-point threat.  Lack of lateral quickness limits his game on both ends.  Lacks the ability to take his man off the dribble and struggles defensively with quicker players.
Late first to early second

He doesn't really look anything like an NBA player.  However, he's been so productive the last three years for Boston College he's hard to overlook.  He's a leader, possesses all the intangibles coaches look for in players and could find a niche coming off the bench on a good NBA team.
A poor man's Shane Battier

I can see why Jordan likes this guy. He plays hard. He plays with passion. He has a great basketball IQ. He doesn't do anything great, but he knows how to play, and his shooting has improved. But I do wonder how well he fits on a team with Walter Herrmann and Adam Morrison.
Does nothing great, but plays with passion.

He's a legit 6-foot-10 with great length and athleticism. Arguably, THE best shot blocker in the country. Has a developing offensive game with some decent moves in the paint and jump shot range out to 15 feet from the basket.

Still very raw on the offensive end.  He has the tools to be a great rebounder, but his numbers don't back it up.  He might be a better rebounder if he didn't try to block every shot launched by an opponent.

Williams has character questions, but there's no questioning his talent.
(Bob Donnan/US Presswire)

Williams has some major offcourt damage control to do. Was dismissed by the team in January for unspecified team violations. Williams has a long history of problems with the team. He was arrested in June, 2005 for marijuana possession and was forced to miss the first eight games of the 2005-06 season for Boston College. Was suspended by the team for the first two games of the 2006-07 season.
Mid to late first round

Williams was having an impressive season before he was dismissed from the team.  The kid already had a ton of character questions, so his dismissal should add fuel to the fire.  But the truth is that scouts have always been in love with his size, athleticism and shot-blocking ability.  As long as his off-court problems aren't too serious (he'll be working out with John Lucas in Houston to help repair his image) it's hard to see an athletic big man like Williams going too long in the draft without hearing his name.  He's a likely mid to late first round pick as long as there are no more character questions still in the closet.

I know there's a risk because of character issues, but this is a great pick for the Nets. Williams delivers exactly what the Nets need -- athleticism, size, shot-blocking, rebounding and toughness. If he had stayed out of trouble, he would've been a lottery pick.
There is a risk, but a great pick talent wise.

A skilled, lithe big man who can score both inside and out.  Good athlete. Very coordinated for someone his size.  Gets off the floor quickly.  Decent shot blocker.  Much improved rebounder.  Good perimeter shooter who has shown some surprising range on his 3-point shot.

Still needs to add another 20 pounds of muscle to handle the rigors of playing in the paint in the NBA.  His lack of strength hurts him at times on the glass.  Struggles defensively against bigger, stronger players.  Tries to do too much at times, leading to a fairly high turnover ratio for a big man.  His consistency is improving, but he still disappears sometimes in big games.

Smith tends to draw a big crowd when he gets the ball down low.
(AP Photo/Jack Dempsey)

Smith announced on April 3rd that he would enter the 2007 NBA Draft, but not hire an agent to preserve his college eligibility.
Lottery to mid first round

A sleeper. Scouts are always looking for skilled big men and they believe Smith has the tools to be a good pro player.  Right now scouts are mixed on his draft status with rankings that go from the late lottery all the way to the late first round.  Workouts will be huge for him as NBA execs have seen him a lot.

The Sixers were eyeing Smith at No. 12. They love his combination of size and athleticism, and they have a gaping hole at power forward. The team got nervous that the Heat would select Smith, so they swapped picks with the Heat and it looks like it cost them some cash -- a small price to pay for the guy they wanted.
Sixers get guy they wanted to fill huge hole.

Has great size and athleticism for the position.  Very competitive.  Sees the floor well. Excellent first step allows him to get deep penetration into the paint.  Great hands.  Rarely mishandles the ball.  Vocal leader on the court. Unselfish.  Good defender.   Doesn't have the rep as a great shooter, but has shot the ball well, especially from deep, for Georgia Tech this year.
Decision making needs to be improved.  He's been very turnover prone.   Needs to add strength. Gets bothered by small, quick guards who pressure him.

Crittenton has a good grip on shooting this season.
(AP Photo/John Bazemore)

Crittenton declared for the NBA Draft on April 25th. Crittenton announced on May 24th that he will hire an agent, ending his college eligibility. Former teammate
of Dwight Howard.
Lottery to mid first round

Most big point guards are really two guards with some ballhandling skills.  Not Crittenton.  He's a legit point guard who has ended the season in a very impressive fashion.  Scouts have cooled in their love affair with big point guards, but Crittenton may just rekindle the romance.

Crittenton is a good fit in L.A. He's a big, physical point guard who can shoot the ball. Phil Jackson likes players like Crittenton. The problem is that he's a few years away from being a major contributor. I'm sure Kobe is thrilled.
Few years away from making an impact.
Super quick guard.  Explosive athlete.  Very difficult to stay in front of.  Has developed a reliable jump shot with three point accuracy.  Excellent in the open court.  Will hit the clutch shot.
Undersized.  Not a pure point guard.  Can get tunnel vision at times. Can play out of control
Late first to early second

Teams think he has NBA speed and quickness, but can he be a full time NBA point guard.  He came up big for Oregon this year which shows some leadership qualities that could get him drafted in the late first round.
Earl Boykins

Brooks is the first real surprise of the draft. He has great quickness and can score the ball, but he is undersized and plays out of control at times. More importantly, how does he fit in Houston? With Mike James, Rafer Alston and Luther Head on the roster, Brooks will be stuck at the end of the bench.
First real surprise, doesn't fit in Houston.

picks.tradeNote: from OKC via WSH and PHI

analysis.text: McRoberts has all the tools to be a good NBA player. The lefty can score inside and out, handle the ball, and defend.  Great passer. A very solid rebounder. He's got good size and an excellent basketball IQ. To top it off, he's an above-average athlete.

Doesn't seem to have a killer instinct.  Often disappears for large stretches. There are some questions about what position he will play in the pros.  Experience and strength continue to be issues.  Isn't particularly quick. Lacks the shooting range that scouts thought he possessed in high school.

McRoberts announced on March 22nd that he was entering the 2007 NBA Draft.
McRoberts has fewer stars to lean on in Durham now.
(Scott Thornton/WireImage.com)
Mid to late first round

McRoberts had a chance to be a Top 10 pick in the 2006 NBA Draft but decided to return to Duke for his sophomore season. His unspectacular sophomore season has caused his stock to plummet.  He played second fiddle to J.J. Redick and Shelden Williams as a freshman ... so scouts expected him to dominate this year.  It didn't happen causing lots of scouts to question if he's really the prospect they though he was coming out of high school.  He looks like a mid to late first rounder at the moment.
A good pick in the second round. McRoberts has an all-around game. He's not a go-to guy, but he is a good passer and rebounder. Kind of a Luke Walton type.
Has an all-round game, think Luke Walton.

picks.tradeNote: from WSH via OKC and HOU

analysis.text: Big-time scorer. Good athlete.  Excellent midrange shooter.  Deep range on his three point shot.  One of the most consistent three point shooters in the draft. Hard worker who can score from just about anywhere on the floor.   Gets to the line a lot and is a solid free throw shooter.
Some questions about his ball handling and in-between game.  Not particularly quick with the ball.  Average defender at best, in part, because of the lack of lateral quickness.
Almond declared for the 2006 NBA Draft, but later withdrew when he could not secure a first-round guarantee.
Mid to late first round

Almond was impressive last year in the Orlando pre-draft camp and was on fire for Rice in his senior season. He may be the best shooter in the draft. He has a good shot at a mid to late first round selection if he can shoot the lights out in workouts.
The Jazz wanted shooting, and they got the guy who is arguably the best shooter in the draft. But what happens to last year's lottery pick, Ronnie Brewer?
Arguably best shooter in draft.

Scoring point guard that has improved in just about every facet of his game.  Has an excellent basketball IQ. He's got great size and strength for the position. He's a good floor general who puts his teammates in a position to score and keeps turnovers to a minimum.  He's a good slasher to the basket, has an excellent midrange jump shot and has shocked scouts with his improvement from three-point range this year.  He's by no means a pure shooter and his mechanics are a little funky, but the ball goes in the basket.  His biggest asset is that he's fearless and not afraid to take clutch shots at the end of the game.

Law doesn't excel at any one thing.  He's a good, but not great, athlete.  He's quick, but not super explosive.  His ability to get to the basket is based more on a knowledge of angles than on sheer quickness.  His jump shot is serviceable, but no one is going to call him a pure shooter.  His defense is acceptable, but doesn't stand out.
Lottery to mid first round

Law has quietly developed into one of the top point guards in the country.  His stellar conference play quickly won over scouts in a draft void of true impact point guards. He has a shot at being one of the first point guards off the board on draft night.

The Hawks finally select a point guard. Law is fearless and ready to play now. I don't think he'll be a star, but he'll be an important part of this team ... unless the team trades this pick. The Hawks have spoken with several teams about trading for a veteran. So we'll see.
Fearless and ready, but not a star.
Polished point guard with great poise.  Fundamentally sound.  Solid shooter.  Great size for the position.  Tough.
A good athlete, but lacks the lateral quickness of most NBA point guards.  Doesn't have deep range on his jump shot.
Plays for the Honka Espoo Playboys in Finland. Averaged 12.7 ppg and 3.9 apg for the Playboys during the 2006-07 season.
Late first to early second

Up and coming prospect who helped himself with a solid showing against Team USA at the Nike Hoop Summit in 2007.  Could be a very interesting late first to early second round pick for someone who can afford to leave him overseas for another year or two.
The Blazers have coveted Kopnen for a while and got him by purchasing another first-round pick. He's a few years away, but he's got a great upside.
Big jump from Finland to NBA, but has upside.
Long, athletic big man with good agility and quickness.  Aggressive. Loves to dunk the ball. Already has a decent NBA body.  Has a decent low-post game from five feet in.
Very raw offensively, especially facing the basket.  NBA executives are looking into a number of off-court issues with Fesenko.
Plays for Mariupol in the Ukraine.  Declared for the 2006 NBA Draft but withdrew when he wasn't given a first-round promise.
Late first to early second
A sleeper thanks to his size and potential.  The question is whether a critical number of NBA decision makers will get a good look before the draft.
Andris Biedrins
He's an athletic big man who has dominated in the Ukraine. Could be one of those international steals down the road. At this point, it's worth the risk.
Could be an international steal down the line.

A long, lanky combo guard who knows how to put the ball in the basket.  Big-time scorer with an excellent 3-point shot.  He's a very smart player, with excellent court vision and a handle that would allow him to play the point occasionally in the NBA.  Good athlete with nice quickness.

Needs to work on his body.  He's thin and doesn't look like he's spent much time in the weight room.  Defense could be an issue.  Can fall in love with his jumper and forget to get to the basket. Streaky shooter thanks to an inconsistent shot release.

Thanks to his long-range shot, Belinelli has a shot at the first round.
(Ales Fevzer/Grazia Neri/Icon SMI)

Plays for Climamio Bologna in Italy. Averaged 12.8 ppg and shot just 32 percent from three in the Euroleague this season. Averaged 16.1 ppg in Italian league play but only shot 33 percent from three there. In 2005-06, averaged 13.4 ppg while shooting 44 percent from three in the Euroleague.
Late first to early second

Belinelli turned heads last season and this summer with very mature play at the highest level of basketball outside the NBA.   His production at the World Championships helped his chances of landing in the first round.  However, he struggled with his shot in the Euroleague this season.  His sweet-shooting stroke has gone cold and Bellinelli shot just 32 percent from three this season.  Scouts still love him, however and think his shooting mechanics are correctable.

Belinelli is one of the best shooters in the draft. He has good size, a lot of athleticism and deep, deep range on his jump shooter. He lit up Team USA last year. In terms of style of play, this is a great fit for the Warriors, though they seem to have a logjam at that position.
Great shooter fits nicely with Warriors.

picks.tradeNote: from MEM via ATL and UTA

analysis.text: Big-time athlete and scorer with great size for the position.  Can break down his defender or hit the jumper.  Excellent range on his 3-point shot.  Has strong leadership qualities.  Good defender.
Injuries gave him a slow start to the season.  May be a little more of a combo guard than a pure point guard.

Can Pruitt run point on an NBA team? (Chris WIlliams/Icon SMI)

Pruitt announced on April 26th that he will declare for the 2007 NBA Draft. Pruitt announced on May 21st that he had hired an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

A sleeper.  A number of NBA scouts commented that they were very intrigued with his play toward the end of the season.  If he can show that he's a legit point prospect, he's going to get a lot of love.   He has all of the rest of the tools.  Should be a mid to late first round pick.
Great pick for the Celtics. Pruitt reminds me a little of Devin Harris and will be a good replacement for the departing Delonte West. He's a combo guard with a great jump shot and good athleticism.
Great pick, will replace West immediately.

Williams is long and smooth. His versatility
will allow him to play the two and three at the next
level -- and maybe even a little point.  Williams is a good midrange shooter.  He's an excellent defender who can guard multiple positions.

His body is very thin.  He needs to continue to add muscle to his frame.  After shooting the ball well from three point range his freshman season, he's been unable to find the mark his sophomore year. Williams is a good athlete, but not a great one.  Lacks explosiveness. Still streaky.  Can look great one minute and disappear the next.
Williams announced on April 5th that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA Draft and would hire an agent, forgoing his junior and senior seasons of college.
Late first to early second

Williams has had a bit of an up and down season this year at Arizona. His decision to stay in school another year hasn't really helped his draft stock.  Right now he's looking like a late first rounder to early second rounder.

Returning for his sophomore year will likely pay off for Williams.
(Reuben Canales/WireImage.com)

Steve Smith
Gifted small forward who excels in the midrange. If he buys into the Spurs' system and learns how to play defense, he could be a steal at this point in the draft.
Could be steal if learns to play defense.

picks.tradeNote: from NO via BOS, DET and POR

analysis.text: Great transition guard who loves to push the tempo of the game.   Excellent NBA body, strength and size for his position.  The lefty turned a somewhat shaky jumper into a reliable offensive weapon his senior year.  Good, physical defender.
Doesn't really excel in any one area.  Not a pure point guard.  Not especially quick or explosive.
Late first to early second
Has drawn scouts attention as a potential second round sleeper.  He had good, but not great, performances at the draft camps, but he's definitely on the NBA radar screen at the moment.

He's long and very skilled.  A big-time scorer. An excellent perimeter shooter.  Range extends out to the 3-point line.  Has really improved his rebounding this season.  Has gotten stronger and seems more comfortable playing around the basket.  Nice jump hook off the right hand box.  Excellent free throw shooter.

His body is getting better, but still needs a lot of work.  He doesn't have the strength to play in the post in the NBA on either end of the floor which has led some scouts to refer to him as a tweener.  His handle isn't great.  He's not unathletic, but he's not a great athlete either.  Runs very stiffly.

Fazekas declared for the 2006 NBA draft, but later withdrew after not getting any real first round interest from NBA teams. Fazekas flirted with declaring for the 2005 NBA draft, but after a disastrous showing in the NCAA Tournament, quickly changed his mind and returned to Nevada for his junior season.
Late first to early second

His added strength and rebounding this season have helped his draft stock considerably, with scouts now wondering whether he's got the skills to be a legit four in the NBA.  He still prefers to play outside-in, but his work on the post this season is giving scouts a reason for hope.

In his final year in Reno, Fazekas looks to improve his stock.
(Aaron M. Sprecher/Icon SMI)

Keith Van Horn
He's Dirk Nowitzki without the athleticism -- a fantastic shooter and a good rebounder. But he has slow, slow feet.
Very slow, but a light's out shooter.

McGuire is a rangy wing player with excellent length and athleticism.  Versatile.  Can play several positions on the floor. Great shot-blocker.  Good ballhandler and playmaker for someone his size.  Good rebounder and defender.

Seriously needs to add strength.  He looks like he has the frame to put on more weight, but struggles both defensively and finishing around the basket because of his lack of strength.  He lacks a consistent perimeter shot and appears to have no real range from the three-point line.  Lacks aggressiveness on the offensive end at times.  Scouts say he has some off-court red flags.
McGuire announced on March 20 that he will enter his name in the 2007 NBA Draft.  McGuire will not hire an agent to keep his draft eligibility.
Late first to early second

McGuire has gotten some media hype, but NBA scouts are wary about how his game will translate in the pros right now.  They think he lacks the maturity to gamble on with a first-round pick.  If he stays in the draft he's a likely second rounder.
He's an interesting prospect. He rebounds and block shots, but he needs to improve his shooting. Kind of a poor man's Andrei Kirilenko.
Needs to improve shot to make an impact.

picks.tradeNote: from GS via CHA, NYK, OKC and ATL

analysis.text: Gray is a legit 7-footer, and he has the girth (he weighs in at 271) to handle the middle full time.  He's a good rebounder, especially on the offensive boards.  Excellent hands.  Good lower body strength helps him hold position in the paint.  Nice baby hook.  Good perimeter shooter.

He's not a very good athlete, and weight has been an issue in the past.  With the NBA moving toward an up-tempo style, Gray's type of game is less valued than it's been in the past.  Not much of a shot blocker.  Poor free throw shooter.

Gray's got the big-man tools to elevate his stock for the 2007 draft.
(Rich Kane/US Presswire)

Gray announced on April 27 that he was declaring for the 2006 NBA draft, but
not hiring an agent to preserve his college eligibility. He later withdrew.
Late first to early second
For a second straight season, Gray continues to prove that he's a legit NBA center prospect, despite scouts' misgivings. He's moved from the first-round bubble to a pretty firm first-round pick.

He's big. He put up good stats in college. But how does he keep up with the speed of the NBA? I'll give him this, though -- he may be the most polished low-post scorer on the Bulls roster, if he makes the team.
Not sure if he can keep up in the NBA.
Scoring point guard with good quickness, a good perimeter shot, good court vision and an excellent defender.  Great experience running an elite team.
Doesn't dominate in any one area.  Not the fastest or quickest point guard.  Barely tall enough.  A good but not great shooter.
Green announced on April 5 that he was declaring for the 2007 NBA draft and forgoing his senior season of college.
Late first to early second
The least sexy of the Gator prospects, but he's been incredibly productive for the Gators over the past two years and saved them more than once.  Right now he's on the first-round bubble.

How many young point guards do the Blazers need? Somebody's getting traded and we don't think it's the two guys the Blazers spent millions to acquire in the last two drafts (Sergio Rodriguez and Petteri Koponen).
Another PG means a trade is inevitable.
Sharp shooting small forward has a pretty stroke from behind the arc.  Has been shooting lights out from three this year.  Good size and length for his position.  An average rebounder.
A little one-dimensional.  Nichols is a spot-up shooter and struggles to shoot off the dribble or coming off screens.   Rarely gets to the free throw line.  Not much of a low-post game to speak of.
Late first to early second

His stock has risen because he's been shooting the ball so well for Syracuse.  The NBA loves big shooters with some athleticism.  But the rest of his game is fairly underdeveloped which puts a ceiling on how high he'll go in the draft.
Nichols is one of the best shooters in the draft. He becomes the ninth player added to the Blazers roster today. Something's gotta give.
9th player added to Blazers roster today.

Excellent athlete with explosive leaping ability.  Strong.  Aggressive around the basket. Works his way to the basket and is a good finisher around the rim.  Has developed a decent midrange jumper.  Excellent, physical defender.
Lacks reliable perimeter skills.  Not much range from three-point line.  Below- average free throw shooter.  Not a great ballhandler.  Undersized for his position.
Late first to early second
A power forward in a two guard's body. Had an excellent season for Wisconsin, but questions about his fit in the NBA continue to hurt his stock.  On the first-round bubble, but teams are intrigued.

Suns were looking at several point guards, so it's surprising to see them pass on guys like Gabe Pruitt for Tucker. He has great experience and can play now, but he can't shoot -- and that seems to be a prerequisite to play for Mike D'Antoni.
Can't shoot, which doesn't fit with Suns.

picks.tradeNote: from CHA via SA, ATL and NYK

analysis.text: GREAT playmaker.  Has an amazing feel for the game.  Makes his teammates better. Excellent basketball IQ.  Leader on the floor. Good rebounder for a guard.  Plays very hard. Has deep range on his jump shot, but he's a streaky shooter.

Not especially quick or athletic.  Doesn't possess an NBA body right now. An average defender at best.  Streaky jump shot. Sometime he tries to do too much, which can lead to turnovers and poor shot selection.
Late first to early second

It's a weak point guard draft and Jordan is one of the few players who is a true point guard.  His stellar play at Marist in his senior season and at the Orlando pre-draft camp has won him some fans (and the inevitable Steve Nash comparisons), but, with that said, he's still a second-round prospect.  Maybe Steve Blake is a more apt comparison.
Jordan was one of the best pure point guards and one of the most enjoyable players in the draft. He lacks size and athleticism, but he has great court vision. Nice pick for the Clippers.
Pure PG who lacks some size.
Smooth point forward with excellent handle and court vision.  Good slashing to the basket.  Good midrange game.
Needs to add strength.  Not a consistent perimeter shooter, especially from deep range.  Lacks experience.
Played in the ABA averaging 13.5 ppg, 10.5 apg and 6 rpg for Beijing Aoshen.  Early entry to the 2006 NBA Draft but withdrew when he didn't get interest from NBA teams.
Second round to undrafted
Impressed scouts at the Orlando pre-draft camp.  He'll intrigue someone in the second round.
A 6-foot-9 point guard who wowed scouts with his ability to handle the ball. In the NBA, he'll be a forward who plays a little like Luke Walton.
Wowed scouts with ball-handling skills.

picks.tradeNote: from PHI via HOU and OKC

analysis.text: A versatile player who can play both the shooting guard and small forward position.  Is a good, albeit streaky, perimeter shooter.   Has good strength at the position.  Is a good defender thanks to his strength and aggressiveness.  Great leadership.

Only an average athlete.  More of a set shooter.  Struggles with accuracy when forced to shoot off the dribble.  Has a funny release on his shot and is slow to let it go which could be a problem at the next level.  Just a so-so ball handler.  Lacks the lateral quickness or ball skills to really get his penetration game going.
Mid to late first round
Has had a solid senior season and NCAA tournament which has him on NBA radar screens.  NBA teams value shooting, so he's got a chance as a late first rounder.
The Sixers will get this pick from Portland. Byars is one of those guys who has all-around talent, but he's not great at any one thing.
All-around talent, but not great.

Tough kid with an excellent motor.  Scrappy.  Excellent midrange shooter.  Not afraid to put it on the floor and take it to the basket.  Good, physical defender.  Emerged this season as a legit 3-point threat.  Good basketball IQ, good feel for the game.
Needs to add strength.  Not a great athlete.  Lacks lateral quickness.  Needs to shore up his consistency from the NBA 3-point line.
Plays for Maroussi Athens.  Averaged 13.5 ppg and shot 47 percent from three.
Late first to early second

He's a proven performer on the international stage which could help his stock.  He's the type of kid that you draft, stash overseas for another year or two and hope he continues to develop.  But he's definitely worth a second- round pick.
Seibutis is a tough 2 guard who can score by slashing to the basket. He'll likely continue to develop in Greece.
A slasher who will develop in Greece.

picks.tradeNote: from ATL via BKN and GS

analysis.text: Prototypical small forward.  Excellent size.  Good athlete.   Good shooter with NBA three point range. Fundamentally sound.
Still developing.  Didn't get a dominant role at UNC.  Struggles putting the ball on the floor.  Doesn't have a take over mentality.
Second round to undrafted
As a prospect he has all the physical tools.  But his lack of production at UNC worries scouts.  Still, as a second round pick, he still has upside.
Very good value pick here. Terry has all the tools to be a good NBA player. He didn't put it together in college, but he might do it in the NBA.
Good value pick, has the tools to succeed.
Long, athletic jumping jack.  Dominant defender. One of the best shot- blockers in college basketball. Excellent rebounder.  Aggressive. Strong.  Excellent quickness for a big man.

Undersized.  Has more of a center's game in a small forward's body.  Raw offensively. He's good dunking the basketball around the basket, but doesn't have much in the way of post moves or a perimeter game.  He doesn't have a great basketball IQ -- mainly because he hasn't been playing basketball for very long.  One of the oldest prospects out there.
Second round to undrafted
NBA scouts love athletic shot-blockers, but there are a lot of question marks about Lasme.
Lasme is one of the better shot-blockers in the draft. He's a little undersized, but he makes up for it with length and athleticism. Another good fit for Golden State.
GS get an undersized shot-blocker.

picks.tradeNote: from MIN via DET and NYK

Still pretty raw and relatively unknown compared to some of the other prospects in the draft.  Needs to add a perimeter game.  He's starting to develop a 10-foot jumper, but it's streaky.

analysis.text: Davidson has the athletic ability and size to be a role player in the NBA.  He's already an excellent shot blocker and rebounder who can fly up and down the floor.  Solid defender.

Scouts have been waiting for him to develop a better offensive game and to gain some weight.  Davidson is too skinny to play in the post at either end at the pro level, and scouts do wonder why he hasn't gained more mass in the past three years at Alabama.  His extra 10 pounds of muscle this summer gives hope that he'll eventually fill out.  Doesn't have a great basketball IQ.

Getting bigger will likely help Davidson's draft stock.
